- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33) in recent days, model tends to underestimate prices; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% for next period.  
- Model consistently underestimates prices after sharp upward spikes (e.g., >70.00) — add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast for 3–5 days post-spike.  
- Model shows persistent lag in capturing mean reversion — if 3–5 consecutive days show price below 65.00, forecast should trend upward toward historical mean (67.5–68.5) over next 7–10 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overcorrects after strong downward moves — reduce forecast slope by 0.1–0.3% per day until sentiment stabilizes.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– cycles (e.g., +0.67, -0.33, +0.67), model tends to misalign with sentiment direction — align forecast slope with sentiment trend, not historical momentum.
